# Ellen West

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v5 c2 P63](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0063)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012)</sub>
- **Origin:** Four Winds  <sub>[v5 c2 P63](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0063)</sub>

## Appearance

Ellen West is a tall, dark, and massive woman with black hair, thick black eyebrows, and slaty dark-blue eyes. She possesses a striking, stately figure and a deep, rumbly, masculine-sounding voice.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P53](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0053), [v5 c13 P7](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0007), [v5 c13 P22](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0022), [v5 c21 P12](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0012)_

## Personality

Ellen is famously stubborn, outspoken, and sincere, with a hearty, gurgling laugh and a sharp sense of humor. Although she has a somewhat grim, forbidding exterior and a fierce temper, she is fiercely protective and devoted to her sister, Rosemary. She is a great reader, intensely interested in world politics, and possesses a sharp, masculine understanding.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P63](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0063), [v5 c13 P7](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0007), [v5 c13 P22](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0022), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 c21 P13](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0013), [v5 c21 P24](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0024)_

- Outspoken and sincere  <sub>[v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025)</sub>

- Skilled at intellectual and political debate  <sub>[v5 c13 P22](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0022), [v5 c22 P1](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0001)</sub>

## Goals

- To keep her sister Rosemary with her so she will never be left alone  <sub>[v5 c21 P20](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0020)</sub>

## History

Ellen West lived for many years with her younger sister, Rosemary, in an old gray house on a hill overlooking Four Winds Harbor. In her youth, she had an affair with Norman Douglas, but after a sharp quarrel he abruptly married another woman. Following the death of their mother, a distraught Ellen coerced Rosemary into swearing on their mother's Bible that neither sister would ever marry or leave the other. Years later, when the widowed Rev. John Meredith proposed to Rosemary, Ellen adamantly refused to release her sister from her oath out of fear of being left alone. However, after Norman Douglas returned to her life and proposed to her, Ellen realized the injustice of her stance and offered to release Rosemary. When Rosemary initially refused to reopen the matter, Ellen declared she would not marry Norman if Rosemary remained alone. Eventually, after the Meredith children smoothed the way between their father and Rosemary, the sisters agreed to a double wedding, and Ellen married Norman Douglas in a September ceremony.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P63](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0063), [v5 c13 P17](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0017), [v5 c15 P29](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0029), [v5 c21 P18](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0018), [v5 c21 P21](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0021), [v5 c22 P12](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0012), [v5 c22 P22](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0022), [v5 c22 P41](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0041), [v5 c34 P39](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0039), [v5 c35 P0](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0000), [v5 c35 P7](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0007)_

## Background by volume

- Daughter of a family of staunch Episcopalians  <sub>[v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066)</sub>
- Lost her father at three years old and her brother at thirteen  <sub>[v5 c21 P17](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0017), [v5 c21 P18](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0018)</sub>
- Jilted by Norman Douglas in her youth after a foolish quarrel  <sub>[v5 c15 P29](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0029), [v5 c21 P18](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0018)</sub>
- Exacted a solemn promise on her mother's Bible from her sister Rosemary that neither of them would ever marry  <sub>[v5 c21 P21](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0021), [v5 c22 P16](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0016)</sub>

## Quotes

> I never had a beau, much less two, and I do not mind now, for being an old maid does not hurt when you get used to it.  <sub>[v5 c1 P10](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0010)</sub>

> Mark my words, Mr. Meredith, that man is going to fight somebody yet. He's aching to. He is going to set the world on fire.  <sub>[v5 c13 P27](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0027)</sub>

> I’m always suspicious of widowers. They are not given to romantic ideas about friendship. They’re apt to mean business.  <sub>[v5 c13 P36](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0036)</sub>

> It’s all very well to be a good Christian, but a body has got to have some common sense.  <sub>[v5 c21 P12](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0012)</sub>

> You promised and you’ve got to keep your word. That’s all.  <sub>[v5 c22 P37](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0037)</sub>
